content:
yuki: Quick heads-up — noticed a regression in canary (2026-03-17 02:12 UTC). /generate median TTFT +18% vs baseline, and kernel attribution shifted: decode kernel now ~58% of token time (was ~32%). linking traces: https://traces.redwood/trace/0x9f3 :warning:

sam: Ugh. Any trigger? we rolled the softbatch heuristic tweak last night (reduce max_wait to 6ms for small routes). Could be batching causing more small microbatches and kernel switching overhead.

yuki: That's my hunch. Sampled a few traces — I see more frequent kernel selector handoffs inside a single token gen. Waterfall looks like extra handoff overhead (~1.8ms per handoff).

anika: Can you paste one of the trace spans? curious about KV cache behavior — are we seeing more cache misses causing kernel fallback to unquantized path?

yuki: Pasted an anonymized span below (sensitive bits removed).

```json
{
  "trace_id":"0x9f3",
  "spans":[
    {"name":"prequeue","dur_ms":0.6},
    {"name":"kernel_select","dur_ms":1.8,"meta":"handoff -> fp16_kernel"},
    {"name":"kvcache_prefetch","dur_ms":0.4,"hit":false},
    {"name":"decode_kernel","dur_ms":5.4},
    {"name":"postproc","dur_ms":0.3}
  ],
  "route":"/generate:small_prompt",
  "batch_size":2
}
```

sam: That kvcache_prefetch hit=false is telling. If prefetch misses, we lose the cheap KV path and force a kernel that does more work. Might explain decode jump.

mike: Also saw more kernel_select calls in the micro-waterfall. If scheduler is splitting a logical request across two microbatches due to strict max_wait, each microbatch triggers selector + prefetch sequence. Multiply that by tokens -> noise.

anika: Proposal: add a "mini-waterfall" panel to the runtime dashboard that aggregates the per-token handoff count distribution (p50/p90/p99) and a heatmap for kvcache hit rate by token position. This will help correlate handoffs -> TTFT.

yuki: Love it. For instrumentation changes I propose the minimal schema below for traces so dashboard queries are easy. We'll tag each span with labels: span.kind=(prequeue|kernel_select|kvcache|kernel_exec), token.index, token.phase=(ttft|decode). Example line: `labels:{"span.kind":"kernel_select","token.phase":"ttft"}`.

sam: If we add token.index at high cardinality, must sample aggressively. Otherwise traces explode. Suggest stratified sampling: keep 100% for routes with high error/TTFT regression, 5% otherwise. Also capture aggregated counters: handoff_count per request, kvcache_miss_count.

anika: Agree. Here's a minimal metric name set to emit from runtime (prom-style):
- runtime_kernel_handoff_total{route,model,phase}
- runtime_kvcache_miss_total{route,model}
- runtime_token_ttft_ms_bucket{route,le}
- runtime_kernel_time_ms_sum{route,kernel_type}
These are easy to wire into dashboards.

mike: For dashboard panels:
- Panel A: TTFT waterfall (stacked bars: prequeue | kernel_select | kvcache | decode) by route, selectable token position window
- Panel B: Kernel handoff distribution (histogram of handoff_count per request)
- Panel C: KV hit heatmap by token.pos x route
- Panel D: Correlation scatter: handoff_count vs p95 TTFT

yuki: I'm going to add a lightweight perf probe to the canary branch that will emit the new labels and counters for one hour. Will also flip sampling to 30% for the impacted route so we get enough traces without blowing storage.

perf-bot: [perf-bot] experiment started: probe=bw-miniwaterfall-2790012345, sampling=30%, routes=[/generate:small_prompt], expires=1h :robot_face:

sam: Nice. After probes run, we should compare two axes: kernel_switch_count and kvcache_miss fraction. If kernel_switch_count explains >60% of TTFT delta, revert the max_wait change or increase batching window for small routes.

anika: Also add an alert: if p95 TTFT increases >12% and kernel_select count p95 increases >20% over baseline within 30m, page oncall.

yuki: Will do. I'll post the dashboard PR and link the probe results here in ~70m. Thanks team. :coffee:
